atoms.text: The slide at Maya’s favourite playground makes a perfect right-angled triangle. The sides of the triangle are made up of a vertical ladder to get to the top of the slide, the slide itself, and the ground.

atoms.a: Which sides would form the right angle in this triangle?
Which side of this triangle would be the longest?

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Jake is trying to hang up paintings on his wall. In order to reach high up on the wall he gets a ladder and leans it against the wall. He notices that this creates a perfect right-angled triangle.

atoms.a: Which side of the triangle would be the hypotenuse?
Which sides would form the right angle in this triangle?
Which side of this triangle would be the longest?

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: An easel is put on a table in a way that forms a perfect right-angled triangle. The sides of the triangle are the support, which runs perpendicular to the table, the table itself and the canvas.

atoms.a: Which side of the triangle would be the hypotenuse?
Which sides would form the right angle in this triangle?
Which side of this triangle would be the longest?

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Elise cuts a brownie diagonally to share with her friend Ali. The new pieces are perfect right-angled triangles. Elise says the longest side of these triangles is where she cut the brownie.

atoms.b: The side she cut became the ((++hypotenuse hypotheses)) of these new triangles, since it is ((++opposite on_the_same_side_as)) the right angle of the cut brownie.
